cases.exposure_context_quote: Empty containers at the scene suggested ingestion of approximately 100 mL of a household permethrin-based insecticide, which was considered likely intentional based on the clinical circumstances.
cases.agent_quote: A 73-year-old woman attempted suicide by ingesting a permethrin-based insecticide.
cases.circumstance: Suicide attempt by ingestion of approximately 100 mL of household permethrin-based insecticide; found at home with decreased consciousness and vomiting.

symptoms.quote: was found at home with decreased consciousness and vomiting.
She exhibited snoring respirations but no stridor or cyanosis. Neurologic examination revealed a Glasgow Coma Scale score of E1V1M4.

symptoms.finding: generalized seizures on hospital days two and three
symptoms.quote: On hospital days two and three, the patient experienced generalized seizures attributed to pyrethroid neurotoxicity.

symptoms.finding: delayed inspiratory stridor and marked laryngeal edema
symptoms.quote: extubation on day eight resulted in inspiratory stridor within 30 minutes. Laryngoscopy demonstrated marked laryngeal edema with impaired vocal cord motion.

cases.time_to_care: Promptly transported to the emergency department by emergency medical services (exact interval UNVERIFIED)

labs.name: initial laboratory findings
labs.value: summarized in Table 1 (values not given in text)
labs.quote: Initial laboratory findings are summarized in Table 1.

treatment.name: endotracheal intubation for airway protection
treatment.quote: Endotracheal intubation was performed to protect the airway, and no laryngeal edema was observed at the time of intubation.

treatment.name: activated charcoal
treatment.quote: Supportive therapies, including activated charcoal administration, were initiated.

treatment.name: reintubation and tracheostomy (day 16)
treatment.quote: Reintubation was required. Repeat laryngoscopy on day 13 revealed persistent edema, and tracheostomy was performed on day 16 due to prolonged airway compromise (Figure 1A).

cases.icu_admission: Yes (mechanical ventilation; weaned day 20) — implied by intubation and ventilation
cases.outcome: Decannulated on day 30 and discharged on day 36 in stable condition
cases.outcome_quote: Her condition gradually improved, she was decannulated on day 30, and discharged on day 36 in stable condition.
cases.notes: Rare delayed-onset (over one week after ingestion) and prolonged (>2 weeks) laryngeal edema requiring tracheostomy.
